item.title: Gates Foundation appoints interim leadership for South and Southeast Asia
item.description: Kalpana Kochhar has been appointed to run South and Southeast Asia for the foundation, whose co-chair Bill Gates recently signalled a shift in focus to human-centric climate investing.

item.title: East Asia seas hit near-record heat as global oceans store more warmth
item.description: Sea surface temperatures in waters around South Korea and across East Asia hit some of their highest levels on record last year, accelerating climate risks to marine ecosystems and the country's fisheries, government data showed.

item.title: Aceh’s bitter lesson, relearned
item.description: In 2004, Aceh was hardest hit by the Indian Ocean tsunami. In 2025, Indonesia’s most disaster-aware province was among the worst hit by floods. The failure was not forecasting, but what happened – or didn’t – after the alarms were raised.

item.title: How to feed ten billion people
item.description: With the world’s population expected to reach ten billion by mid-century, agriculture must produce more with less – every season, everywhere. The knowledge and tools to end and prevent food insecurity are already in hand, but they have yet to be used wisely and at scale.

item.title: Asylum seekers brace for bleak 2026 as countries clamp down
item.description: Protections shrink for refugees and asylum seekers as leaders from Donald Trump in the US to Britain's Keir Starmer toughen rules.

item.title: Adopting low-cost ‘healthy’ diets could cut food emissions by one-third
item.description: Choosing the “least expensive” healthy food options could cut dietary emissions by one-third, according to a recent study.

item.title: Singapore expands emissions registry to boost corporate carbon reporting
item.description: The expanded emissions database comes ahead of a regulatory mandate for listed companies to report Scope 3 emissions this financial year.

item.title: Japan sets 2026 price band for carbon market to steer investment by big polluters
item.description: Scheme will cover up to 400 major emitters and set a floor and ceiling on CO2 prices ahead of 2027 market launch.

item.title: Asia is the world’s biggest spender on nature, but it must invest billions more: UNEP
item.description: For every $1 going to nature globally, $30 is spent on destructive activities, a new report found. Southeast Asia alone will need to increase nature financing by sevenfold annually by 2030 to meet global targets.

item.title: Asian state-owned companies dominate global carbon emissions: study
item.description: Chinese and Indian coal and oil firms accounted for about one third of global fossil fuel emissions in 2024, according to data from InfluenceMap. More than half of major Asian producers increased emissions that year, driven mainly by coal.
